PHARMACOGENOMICS PANEL W/CLS REPORT
This assay includes targeted testing for specific variants in the following genes/loci: ABCG2, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CYP4F2, DPYD, F5, HLA-
A*31:01, HLA-B*15:02, HLA-B*57:01, HLA-B*58:01, IFNL3, NAT2, NUDT15, SLCO1B1, TPMT, UGT1A1, and VKORC1.
This report summarizes the best interpretation of genomic information by Quest Diagnostics. It is not a substitute for physician advice or clinical judgment and does not take into account
all possible variables that may have an effect on various drug responses. No clinical decisions should be made based solely on the information contained in this report.

leaving the Quest Diagnostics reporting environment. Quest Diagnostics does not control the content of the CLS website. All clinical annotations and medical guidance provided on
the CLS website are generated by CLS professional staff. The CLS report, and the information contained therein, is neither reviewed, approved, endorsed by, or affiliated with Quest
Diagnostics and all information contained in the CLS report is the sole responsibility of CLS. Any questions pertaining to the content of the CLS report should be directed to CLS. The CLS
report should only be used in conjunction with professional clinical judgement, clinical expertise and the overall assessment of additional factors that may influence medication response.
Clinical decisions should not be made solely using the information contained in the CLS report. It is recommended that the clinician consult regularly with CLS for important updates to
clinical annotations and medical guidance.
Please note that in some instances, variants and/or genes tested for by Quest Diagnostics and included in this report may not be included in the CLS report.

Genomic DNA is extracted and amplified by both whole genome amplification and multiplex PCR to overcome the complexities associated with genotyping homologous pharmacogenetic
genes. Amplification products are fragmented, purified and subsequently applied to a genotyping microarray. Hybridization, staining, washing, and imaging are completed as part of an
automated process. The genotypes for two DPYD variants [c.868A>G and c.2279C>T] are determined in a separate PCR analysis. Genotype analysis includes allele translation and, if
applicable, copy number analysis. This assay cannot detect variants in unexamined gene regions, or variants in other untested genes.
For technical reasons, genotyping for the CYP2C9*8 allele is done indirectly. The CYP2C9*8 allele is defined by the c.449G>A (rs7900194) variant, but in this assay, CYP2C9*8
genotyping is performed by testing for the c.-1766T>C (rs9332094) variant which is in strong linkage disequilibrium with the c.449G>A (rs7900194) variant. The c.-1766T>C (rs9332094)
variant is used as a proxy to infer the presence or absence of the c.449G>A (rs7900194) variant, but the association between these variants is not absolute. Therefore, both false
negative and false positive results for CYP2C9*8 are possible. False negative and false positive results for CYP2C9*8 are expected to be rare. Correlation of CYP2C9 test results with
clinical findings is recommended.
Diplotypes and phenotypes are determined exclusively from the alleles or variants interrogated by this test. In certain instances, more than one diplotype may be possible. In these
instances, an assignment of diplotype will be made using the best available phasing data from the medical and scientific literature, and guidelines from pharmacogenomic expert panels.
In instances where a single diplotype cannot be assigned, multiple diplotypes will be reported. An allele that is negative for the variants tested for by this assay is inferred to be the wild
type or *1 (normal activity) allele.
In the event of an unsuccessful genotyping result, the associated allele or variant will not be included in the "alleles tested" section of the report. Duplications of the CYP2D6 gene
are detected, but this assay cannot determine the identity of the duplicated allele(s), nor can it determine the precise number of copies. When a CYP2D6 duplication is identified, the
prediction of phenotype is based on the best available data for allele copy number. As a result, there could be discordance between the phenotype prediction and an individual's clinical
phenotype when a duplication of the CYP2D6 gene is present. This test is not intended to detect mosaicism if present. In some situations, additional genetic testing may be appropriate.
Results should be interpreted by a healthcare professional in the context of clinical findings, relevant history, and other laboratory data to guide the development of any therapeutic
plans. Patients should not change their medications without communicating with their health care providers. Differences between clinical and interpretive test results may be due to
untested genes and/or variants not included in this assay or environmental factors such as drug-drug interactions. Other factors such as lifestyle, age, gender, diet or liver, and/or kidney
dysfunction may also affect drug metabolism.
Annotation of the variant(s) identified reflects the current state of Quest Diagnostics' understanding at the time of this report. In general, interpretations are based on published literature
and existing guidelines. Variant interpretation may change for a variety of reasons, including but not limited to, updates in guidelines and availability of additional scientific and clinical
information. Medical inquiry regarding potential changes to the variant interpretation is strongly recommended prior to making any clinical decision.
For questions regarding variant interpretation, please call Quest Diagnostics at 866-GENEINFO (436-3463) to speak to a genetic counselor or laboratory director.
This test was developed and its analytical performance characteristics have been determined by Quest Diagnostics. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. This assay has been
validated pursuant to the CLIA regulations and is used for clinical purposes.
For additional information, please refer to http://education.questdiagnostics.com/faq/FAQ206 (This link is being provided for informational/educational purposes only.)
